label: Merlot
value: Very widespread, especially on the right bank of Bordeaux (Saint-Émilion, Pomerol), it produces supple, round wines with notes of red and black fruits. It is also highly valued for its soft tannins.

label: Cabernet Sauvignon
value: The king grape variety of Bordeaux’s left bank (Médoc, Graves), it yields powerful, tannic wines with aromas of blackcurrant, bell pepper, and cedar. It offers excellent aging potential.

label: Syrah
value: Cultivated mainly in the northern Rhône Valley (Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage), it produces full-bodied, spicy wines, often marked by notes of violet and pepper.

label: Grenache
value: Present in the southeast (Southern Rhône, Languedoc, Roussillon), it produces rich, warm wines, often blended with Syrah and Mourvèdre. It also goes into the composition of many rosés.

label: Gamay
value: Beaujolais grape variety, light and fruity.

label: Malbec
value: Cahors treasure, with intense and fleshy aromas.

label: Carignan
value: formerly widely planted in the south, it is making a strong comeback in quality winemaking.

label: Chardonnay
value: A universal grape variety but emblematic of Burgundy (Chablis, Meursault, Puligny…), it can yield very mineral wines or, conversely, rich and oaky ones. It is also a pillar of Champagne.

label: Sauvignon Blanc
value: Very present in the Loire (Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé) and Bordeaux, it yields lively, fruity wines with notes of citrus and boxwood.

label: Riesling
value: Very distinctive in Alsace, it produces taut, floral wines, sometimes with petrol notes with age, and endowed with a beautiful acidity.

label: Chenin Blanc
value: Typical of the Loire (Vouvray, Montlouis, Anjou), it is very versatile: dry, sweet, luscious, or even sparkling. It offers great aromatic complexity.

label: Viognier
value: cultivated in the northern Rhône Valley (Condrieu), it delivers intense aromas of white flowers, apricot, and peach.

label: Muscat
value: fragrant, often vinified as a vin doux naturel (Rivesaltes, Beaumes-de-Venise).

label: Colombard
value: typical of the Southwest, used for fresh and fruity white wines.
